source_text:
τίς τῶν ἀρχαίων ἐπισκόπων Χριστὸν
ἀτιμάσας ἐζωγράφησεν; τίς τὸν Ἀβραὰμ καὶ Ἰσαὰκ καὶ Ἰακώβ, Μωυσέα τε καὶ τοὺς
προφήτας ἢ Πέτρον ἢ Ἀνδρέαν ἢ Ἰάκωβον ἢ Ἰωάννην ἢ τοὺς λοιποὺς ἀποστόλους
οὕτως παρεδειγμάτισεν καὶ ἐθριάμβευσεν; 24 ἅμα δὲ καὶ ψεύδονται, ἐξ ἰδίας αὐτῶν
ἐννοίας μορφὰς τῶν ἁγίων ἄλλως καὶ ἄλλως ἀνατυποῦντες, ποτὲ μὲν γέροντας ποτὲ
δὲ νεωτέρους τοὺς αὐτοὺς*, ἃ μὴ ἑωράκασιν ἐμβατεύοντες. κόμην γὰρ ἔχοντα τὸν
σωτῆρα γράφουσιν ἐξ ὑπονοίας διὰ τὸ Ναζωραῖον αὐτὸν καλεῖσθαι, ἐπείπερ οἱ
Ναζιραῖοι κόμας ἔχουσιν.
Σφάλλονται δὲ οἱ τοὺς τύπους αὐτῷ συνάπτειν πειρώμενοι· οἶνον γὰρ ἔπινεν
ὁ σωτήρ, ὃν οἱ Ναζιραῖοι οὐκ ἔπινον. 25 οὐ πρέπον ... ἐστὶ θεὸν ἔχειν ἡμᾶς ἐν
χρώμασι καὶ μέλεσι ζωγραφούμενον.
thought_title: No ancient bishop painted Christ or the saints
orientation: Epiphanius is asking the emperor whether any ancient bishop ever painted Christ or the saints, and is beginning to explain why painters who do so are inventing false appearances.
pass_a_gloss: Which of the ancient bishops, having dishonored Christ, painted [him]? Which [of them] thus made a public example of and triumphed over Abraham and Isaac and Jacob, and Moses and the prophets, or Peter or Andrew or James or John or the remaining apostles? 24 And at the same time they also lie, from their own thought forms of the saints differently and differently fashioning, sometimes old men, sometimes younger the same ones, entering into things which they have not seen. For having long hair the Savior they paint from conjecture because [of] his being called Nazorean, since the Nazirites have long hair. But they go astray, those trying to attach the types to him; for wine the Savior drank, which the Nazirites did not drink. 25 It is not fitting ... for us to have God in colors and limbs painted.

choices.english: made a public example of and triumphed over
choices.why: The two verbs together describe public disgrace; 'made a public example of' keeps the shaming force of παραδειγματίζω, and 'triumphed over' keeps the military procession image of θριαμβεύω.

The phrase is repeated later in the letter; 'thought' keeps the singular idea of a private mental invention, matching the brief's 'from their own imagination' without using the banned 'imagination' for μορφὰς.
The brief's glossary requires 'forms' for μορφὰς and bans 'likenesses'.
The verb means going into or intruding upon what one has not seen; 'entering into' keeps the spatial image of trespassing into unseen things.

choices.english: to attach the types to him
choices.why: τύπους here means the Nazirite hair customs or patterns; 'types' keeps the technical sense of a pattern or model, and 'attach' keeps the idea of wrongly connecting them to Christ.
rejected: to connect the figures to him
to join the models to him

choices.why: The source has a gap; the gloss marks the missing text with ellipsis and keeps the surviving words exactly.

pass_b_english: Which of the ancient bishops dishonored Christ by painting him? Which of them made a public example of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, of Moses and the prophets, of Peter or Andrew or James or John or the rest of the apostles, and paraded them in triumph in this way? At the same time they are lying, fashioning forms of the saints from their own thought in different ways—sometimes making the same ones old men, sometimes younger—entering into things they have never seen. They paint the Savior with long hair based on conjecture, because he is called a Nazarene, since Nazirites have long hair. But those who try to connect the types to him go astray, for the Savior drank wine, which Nazirites did not drink. It is not fitting for us to have God painted in colors and limbs.
notes: The source has a gap after οὐ πρέπον in the clause 'οὐ πρέπον ... ἐστὶ θεὸν ἔχειν ἡμᾶς ἐν χρώμασι καὶ μέλεσι ζωγραφούμενον'; the gloss marks the missing text with ellipsis and does not supply it.

problems.quote: and triumphed over them in this way
problems.why: Greek says they mocked or made a spectacle, not that they triumphed over them; adds a meaning not present.
problems.fix: and mocked them in this way

edits.old: and triumphed over them in this way
edits.new: and mocked them in this way

fixed: Changed 'and triumphed over them in this way' to 'and mocked them in this way' because the Greek παρεδειγμάτισεν means 'made a public example of' or 'mocked', not 'triumphed over'.

problems.why: ἐθριάμβευσεν means 'triumphed over' in the sense of leading a triumphal procession of captives, a stronger military/shaming image than 'mocked'.
problems.ruling: ἐθριάμβευσεν denotes triumphal humiliation; “mocked” loses the triumphal/shaming nuance.

problems.why: τύπους here means 'outward forms/appearances' (physical features), not 'types' in the theological sense; painters are attaching physical characteristics to Christ.
problems.ruling: τύπους here refers to outward forms/figures, not theological “types”; translation misleads.

edits.old: and mocked them in this way
edits.new: and led them in triumph in this way

fixed: Changed 'mocked them' to 'led them in triumph' because ἐθριάμβευσεν means 'triumphed over' in a triumphal procession sense, not merely 'mocked'.
Changed 'types' to 'forms' because τύπους here refers to outward physical appearances, not theological types.

problems.quote: led them in triumph in this way
problems.why: ἐθριάμβευσεν means 'paraded in triumph' (shaming captives), not 'led them in triumph' as honor.
problems.fix: paraded them in triumph like this
problems.ruling: ἐθριάμβευσεν connotes triumphal parade of captives, not honor; “led them in triumph” misleads.

problems.quote: those who try to attach the forms to him
problems.source_quote: οἱ τοὺς τύπους αὐτῷ συνάπτειν πειρώμενοι
problems.why: τύπους here means 'types/patterns' (Nazirite customs as type), not 'forms' (already used for μορφάς).
problems.fix: those who try to connect the types to him
problems.ruling: τύπους means “types”/typology, not visual “forms”; translation obscures intended meaning.

edits.old: and led them in triumph in this way
edits.new: and paraded them in triumph in this way

edits.old: those who try to attach the forms to him
edits.new: those who try to connect the types to him

fixed: ἐθριάμβευσεν means 'paraded in triumph' (shaming captives), not 'led them in triumph' as honor; changed to 'paraded them in triumph in this way'.
τύπους here means 'types/patterns' (Nazirite customs as type), not 'forms' (already used for μορφάς); changed to 'connect the types to him'.
